question: 00_07 HW.23 — 106's bonded interface read as a pressed frictional contact: the friction it needs, where it opens and the growth pressure that keeps it closed (step 1, a validity map)

inputs.share_106: mechanical/gyroid_wood_strain_share.json — its lattice reading, grids and the cells of both its groups; σᴵ is not in it, so it is recomputed here with 106's functions (importlib, no main()) and the shares held to every cached cell of both groups

groups.union: both groups; the binding claim and the junction ceiling as 106's consumer blocks name them

inputs.p0_source: Bruder G. R. 1998, Finite-Elemente-Simulationen und Festigkeitsanalysen von Wurzelverankerungen, Dissertation Universität Karlsruhe (TH), Wissenschaftliche Berichte FZKA 6206, Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe; doi 10.5445/IR/67698 (DataCite record read 2026-10-22: creator, title, 1998, doctoral thesis)

turgor_free_root_cells.is: the turgor of free-lying root cells, cited by Bruder from his ref [27] (secondary; p. 100 repeats it as «als typischer Wert 0,5 MPa») — a cell's internal pressure, not a pressure measured on a body

spring_clamps_on_poplar_roots.quote: bis zu 0,72 MPa bei etwa 2 mm Dickenzuwachs
spring_clamps_on_poplar_roots.is: Bruder's own first field test («in einem ersten Feldversuch»): 15 spring clamps (5, 10 and 20 N/mm) on thin poplar roots (< 10 mm), read after about 2 years at about 2 mm of radial growth — the largest over the clamps («bis zu»); compliance-limited, not a stall pressure against a rigid body, and whether it rises further Bruder left open; a broadleaf's root, not a conifer's stem callus

p0_excluded.why: ambiguous in Bruder, so not taken (00_07 HW.23 step (1): «2.5 МПа» не брати): p. 15 gives it for roots impeded in their expansion, measured indirectly, from his ref [28], open-ended above («und darüber»); p. 100 gives it as the soil strength at which root growth stops, from his ref [86], cross-referenced to the p. 15 section — two senses, one an indirect lower end, the other a stopping strength

p0_further_on_the_pages.is: root figures on the same pages that the leg does not take (secondary in Bruder): set against the p₀ each statement needs, never used as a reading

inputs.p0_domain: ROOT growth pressure (poplar roots and root cells) — no primary found in reach (2026-10-22) measures a conifer's stem callus pressing on an inclusion; p₀ taken uniform, sustained and shear-free (OUR reading); neither p₀ nor μ is picked — each statement prints the p₀ it needs
inputs.strain_source: 105's cache: stem_readings_87 (87's source day — one Scots pine, DBH 21.5 cm, one January day) × depth_fraction
inputs.sign_convention: σ_n tension positive; contact pressure p₀ − σ_n; opening where σ_n ≥ p₀; s = +1 the wood at the anchor in tension (windward), −1 in compression (leeward)

axial_anode_bond_force_105.adds_to: on a smooth envelope |τ| = √(τ_ψ² + τ_R²) ≥ |τ_ψ| at every point: the bond force can only raise the friction that contact needs

psi_resolution.is: a one-cell patch of the envelope spans this arc of ψ; the homogenised traction equals the patch average only to leading order in cell/radius, so the ψ-resolved open shares and μ maxima carry an unquantified O(cell/radius) error

homogenisation: the traction is the average over the cut lattice on the envelope; for a SMOOTH contact whose local normal is the envelope's, full stick needs |τ_loc| ≤ μ·p_loc at every point, so μ_req of the averages is a lower bound on the friction it needs and an averaged opening forces a local one — that contact can be shown failing, never holding. A contact that is not smooth has no guaranteed direction (an inclined facet carries averaged shear with zero friction, an undercut one averaged tension under positive pressure), and with tissue in the macropores (01_04 §2, Phase 2) the envelope is crossed by an interlocked composite: the traction is its demand, and neither failing nor holding follows. On a Voigt cell σᴵ is a bound tensor's stress, not the average of an admissible local traction
not_computed: the unbonded and the interlocked ends — slip with the normal contact kept, opening, and the internal Ti–tissue faces of an interlock — and what each does to t_L (the leg's step 2: a slipping interface keeps no uniform field in an anisotropic matrix)
the traction on the ligament ends and on the ligament surfaces inside the pores (the homogenised traction is their average), and the O(cell/radius) error of that average
the Ø15 interface, callus against the old wood of the drilled wall — no interface in 106's model
p₀ for a conifer's stem callus, its distribution around the gyroid and its relaxation
the finite length: the ends' axial shear and the anode bond force's distribution along the gyroid
C44, the tissue's stiffness, the bark and S5 — as in 106
verdict: Read as a SMOOTH contact on the gyroid's envelope — its local normal the envelope's, pressed by a growth pressure p₀ and held by friction, with no adhesion — the bonded field of 106 is carried around the interface by normal traction and in-plane shear; the infinite cylinder's axial shear is zero. With a cube axis on the stem's axis (θ = 0, free of C44) the tension half stays closed at the source day's strain (676–1837 µε at the gyroid) only under p₀ of at least 5.14 MPa (the Scots pine group) ⊥ 1.75 MPa (the green group) — 2.4× the higher named root reading (0.72 MPa, Bruder's clamps; the turgor reading is 0.5 MPa); the 2.5 MPa Bruder uses in two senses is not taken; the green group's lowest need lies below it, and the highest further root figure on his pages (1.45 MPa) stays below the lowest p₀ needed. On both named readings the tension half's averaged traction exceeds p₀ at both ends of the day in every one of its 180 cells (the Scots pine group; 60 bare lattice) and every one of its 468 cells (the green group; 156 bare lattice) — an opening only where the envelope is a smooth contact; with tissue in the pores, a tension that only adhesion or the interlock could carry; it opens the poles facing along the stem above 29–95 µε (the Scots pine group) ⊥ 44–277 µε (the green group), and at half that strain the friction needed is already at least 0.34–0.39 (no p₀). In the compression half the poles facing around the stem open above 276 µε at the earliest, and where they stay closed at the source day's strain the friction needed is at least 0.68–73.63. Off the axis the pole traction falls as C44 falls: the tension half stays closed at the source day's strain only below a Zener ratio of 0.035 on some install angle, against the Voigt ceiling 4.402; no measured C44 is used. At 106's binding cell (the union's lowest θ = 0 share, a Voigt phase-bound cell whose σᴵ is a bound tensor's stress) such a contact would open at least 17.4× below the binding strain (Ta), and would stay closed up to it only under p₀ ≥ 12.5 MPa. At the union's C44 → 0 supremum the in-plane stress is isotropic — the bending field puts no averaged in-plane shear there, which is no holding claim; its tension half opens at the source day's upper whisker on a large stem on 2 of 2 named readings and at its median on a DBH-38 bark on 1. With tissue in the macropores (01_04 §2, Phase 2) the lattice interlocks with it: the envelope traction is then the demand on that composite, and neither failing nor holding follows from it; what opening, slip and interlock do to the share is not computed.
